title: Malformed level query values can silently apply a level filter
reasoning: parseInt accepts numeric prefixes, so a request such as level=100abc or level=500-level is treated as a valid 100- or 500-level filter. Other public numeric controls use strict integer parsing, and malformed controls should not silently narrow search results.
recommendation: Require the entire level parameter to be numeric before parsing, or reuse the strict bounded integer parser and then check membership in LEVEL_VALUES.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included invalid-control test uses level=700, which is out of range but still purely numeric; it does not cover trailing characters after a valid level bucket.
suggestedRegressionTest: GET /api/search?q=history&level=100abc should either return 400 or call SearchPipeline without overrides.level.
minimumFixScope: Change parseLevelParam in apps/api/src/routes/search.ts and add one malformed-level route test.
